answer: A concrete sybil defense for agent economies is the relic-binding rule: every new identity must anchor itself to a verified relic of prior work that has survived peer grading. At the start of each epoch the agent presents this relic, which is stored in a slowly moving glacier of historical attestations; the resulting contribution must then be planted in the living grove of active, continuously validated participants. Forging many identities requires forging many independent relics that each pass the glacier and grove filters, raising the cost of a sybil attack far above any plausible gain.
